purpose: Record read-only primary-source inspection supporting a conceptual Codex implementation and an adapted audit; does not attest reproducibility of the original DAS generator.

project.name: Deep Academic Survey (DAS)
project.paper_title: Deep Academic Survey: Stateful Agentic Closed-Loop Paradigm for Academic Survey Automation
project.generation_code_status: Not publicly present at inspected commit: DAS/ contains only README.md announcing future release
project.implementation_relationship: Conceptually informed independent implementation; not official DAS, not a complete reproduction, no benchmark-equivalence claim.

inspection.mode: Read-only HTTPS retrieval and targeted source inspection
inspection.hash_scope: Exact bytes returned by pinned raw-file HTTP requests; web page hashes identify retrieved HTML bytes and may change with page chrome.
inspection.inspected_materials: Project HTML, versioned paper HTML, GitHub commit/tree metadata, pinned README/protocol/schema files and evaluator code. Python source was read and hashed, never run.

sources.used_for: Author project landing page and primary-resource links
Sections 3 and Appendices B, C, E: workflow, source-access boundary and stated evaluation protocol
Method overview, release scope, evaluation families and literature lake coverage
Evaluation package layout and published comparison conventions
Four families, sixteen criterion names, evidence inputs and score aggregation
Benchmark-specific candidate pool and output conditions, excluded from generic workflow defaults
Reusable paper representation groups; public schema is not a source-entailment guarantee
Citation evidence cards, assessability calibration, year filter, sampling and citation-distribution separation
Visible-artifact judge boundary, page sampling and rubric
Discourse/taxonomy rubric, active PDF/image payload path and parsing safeguards
Preprocessing boundaries; not adopted as a skill dependency
Stage execution behavior; completion is not proof of valid evaluation
Upstream code/documentation license; no upstream implementation copied

verified_boundaries.claim: Core generation implementation is not released at the pinned commit
verified_boundaries.scope: Status as inspected; may change later

verified_boundaries.claim: The manuscript Reviewer described in Appendix C.4 does not read source papers and is not a source-level entailment verifier
verified_boundaries.scope: Paper-described generation role, not all possible review tools

verified_boundaries.claim: The BSC paper-content judge consumes compact abstract/metadata evidence cards rather than full paper evidence
verified_boundaries.scope: Citation semantic assessment can be limited by missing or compressed source details

verified_boundaries.claim: The BSC reference-map filter defaults to arXiv years 2020 through 2026 and is called by the topic payload builder
BSC separates unavailable evaluator evidence from demonstrated manuscript defects
verified_boundaries.scope: Prompt convention; workbench retains explicit unassessable status instead of treating neutral score as verified

verified_boundaries.claim: MAR evaluates visible artifact presentation and explicitly excludes scientific correctness
verified_boundaries.scope: Rendered page evidence and declared sampling only

verified_boundaries.claim: The active TSQ/HDQ runtime path sends full PDF or rendered images; local configuration can limit images to the first pages
verified_boundaries.scope: Presence of Markdown/cap helpers does not prove they are active inputs to this path

verified_boundaries.claim: Evaluation preprocessing disables formula recognition, and the generation metadata extraction described in the paper removes some trailing materials
verified_boundaries.scope: Evaluation preprocessing and offline metadata extraction are distinct processes

verified_boundaries.claim: Runner can continue after an evaluation stage failure
verified_boundaries.scope: A finished process is not evidence of valid completed score outputs

documentation_discrepancies.observation: Protocol says frozen evaluator prompts are not part of the current release; pinned Python evaluator files contain metric-specific judge prompts.
documentation_discrepancies.handling: Use inspected code to describe present capabilities; do not claim the public documentation package is fully synchronized.

documentation_discrepancies.observation: Long forms for HDQ and MAR differ across artifacts (Discourse versus Drafting; Assembly versus Artifact).
documentation_discrepancies.handling: Use family identifiers BSC/TSQ/HDQ/MAR and the adapted checklist; do not imply those naming differences define separate metrics.

adaptation_choices: Preserve explicit literature, organization, writing and assembly states without requiring multiple agents or a large lake.
Add source-aware claim verification beyond manuscript discourse review.
Leave specialist rule packs and maintained-library adapters outside the generic core.
Use DOI/other identities and older/non-arXiv sources when relevant; no inherited hard year/provider filter.
Use null plus unassessable or not_applicable for missing audit input or out-of-scope deliverables; no missing-score imputation.
Label audit outputs adapted-workbench-v1; do not compare adapted scores directly with published DAS-Eval totals.
Expose evidence coverage, changed dependencies, scoped repair and unresolved findings separately from structural success.
refresh_policy: Re-fetch the public release statement and record a new commit/hash set before updating claims about upstream code availability. If rubric or payload behavior changes, version the adapted profile and retain the previous run's identity.
